title: The Pulse, Thursday 2 October 2026
tldr: Claude Code gets mods—TypeScript plugins that change behavior and UI, built by Claude or handwritten. Cloudflare's Clef decision models launch with an RL fine-tuning platform on Workers. arXiv delivered overnight: voice-agent document grounding, agentic coding under RL, and agent memory.

models.title: Apodex 1.1 Mini (free)
models.summary: Reasoning-first model for long-horizon research and forecasting, works with files, data, code, and tools, 262k context, free.
models.why: Free 262k reasoning model: fits Mackinac legislative research before we pay for a bigger one.

models.title: Pareto 26.10 Preview
models.summary: Composite multimodal model: runs several models per request, evaluates answers, returns the best one. 1M context, $0.80 / $3.20 per million tokens.
models.why: Multi-model voting behind one call: could replace a DSPy judge ensemble with one model that does it internally.

research.title: DuplexSpeechBench-Document Grounding: Benchmarking Document Grounding and Hallucinations in Voice Agents
research.summary: Benchmark for document grounding in voice agents across five professional domains, tests three failure modes (context saturation, instruction conflict, fabrication).
research.why: We grade EverRaise voice agents on grounding accuracy; a specialized benchmark tells us whether the general eval is missing anything.

research.title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
research.summary: RL on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes the last-mile gap: dropped requirements, incomplete test coverage, broken behavior. Tests cross-benchmark transfer.
research.why: Coding agents that test themselves incompletely and break existing behavior are the current bottleneck for autonomous PRs.

research.title: MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory
research.summary: Long-term memory system for conversational agents: bypasses costly LLM-driven memory organization and consolidation, optimizes write operations.
research.why: Botterfly's Mnemosyne does exactly this; a paper on memory consolidation costs validates the design target.

research.title: Beyond Leaderboards: Tokenomics of Agentic Small Language Model Ensembles
research.summary: Evaluates SLM-judge-mediated agentic ensembles on operational reliability, cost, latency, and token efficiency, not just accuracy.
research.why: Our wehshi PR review panel runs three models with a judge; a tokenomics framework tells us where the cost is and whether cheaper models change it.

research.title: LawCompass: Navigating from Legal QA to Multi-Agent Deep Research with Grounded Evidence
research.summary: Multi-agent system for legal research: systematic evidence retrieval, multi-step reasoning, grounded answers. Moves beyond conversational QA.
research.why: Pipeline's nonprofit clients need grounded policy research; a legal multi-agent pattern is one model for similar legislative workflows.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.49.0
releases.summary: Org-level analytics view, ingestion overview route, tool filters on session table, evaluator onboarding tracking.
releases.why: We trace SalesKick and EverRaise flows through Langfuse; org-level ingestion stats and tool filters make debugging multi-service flows faster.

hackernews.title: Clef: Open-weight decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
hackernews.summary: Cloudflare launches Clef, open-weight decision models (Yes/No/Confidence), and an RL fine-tuning platform on Workers.
hackernews.why: Decision models can gate agent actions live; an RL fine-tuning platform on Workers fits our serverless edge deployment pattern.

hackernews.title: RIP, vector database
hackernews.summary: Turbopuffer argues vector databases are becoming unnecessary: purpose-built compute plus object storage beats them on cost and latency.
hackernews.why: We run Pinecone for Mackinac; if the economics flipped we could swap it for cheaper cloud-native storage before we scale further.

hackernews.title: GPT-Synopsys: Frontier Intelligence to Revolutionize Chip Design
hackernews.summary: OpenAI and Synopsys announce GPT-Synopsys, frontier models for chip design workflows.
hackernews.why: No direct use for us yet, but another vertical reasoning model worth watching: if chip design can ship one, legal and policy research will too.

x_posts.title: Claude Code mods
x_posts.summary: Claude Code now supports mods: TypeScript plugins that customize behavior, UI, and features. Write them by hand or have Claude build them.
x_posts.why: Hermes and Claude Code are both agent runtimes; mods are the same extensibility layer we built with skills, but shipped as a first-class plugin system.

x_posts.title: claude.dev launches
x_posts.summary: Anthropic launched claude.dev: developer docs, performance deep dives (made the web app 3x faster), Opus 5.5 effectiveness guide, eval hillclimbing.
x_posts.why: Performance optimization and eval automation guides: both apply to Chrysalis and our own agent evals.

x_posts.title: Fine-tuned Qwen3 4B beats Claude Sonnet 4.6
x_posts.summary: Fine-tuned Qwen3 4B on AWS outperforms both the base model and Claude Sonnet 4.6 on a specific task, cheaper and faster.
x_posts.why: We run Sonnet for SalesKick grading; task-specific fine-tuning at 4B could drop cost and latency if the quality holds on our own evals.

closing: Python releases: nothing in the window.
